questions.q: How did the master and mistress treat animals and people?
choices: They were good and kind to everybody and everything
They were kind to their own horses but not to others
They were strict and stern with nearly everyone
They cared about people but not much about animals
questions.evidence: they were good and kind to everybody and everything

questions.q: What had the squire and Farmer Grey worked for more than twenty years to get rid of?
choices: Check-reins on the cart-horses
Blinkers on the carriage horses
Fox hunting across their fields
Cruel whips used in the village
questions.evidence: to get check-reins on the cart-horses done away with

questions.q: What did the mistress do when she met a heavily laden horse with its head strained up?
choices: She got out and reasoned with the driver
She offered the carter money to buy the horse
She sent John to fetch a policeman
She told John to drive past quickly
questions.evidence: reason with the driver in her sweet serious voice

questions.q: What did Sawyer do when his pony turned toward the park gates?
choices: Wrenched its head round and lashed it with the whip
Let it trot on into the park and right up to the house
Patted its neck and turned it round gently
Got down from the cart and led it on foot
questions.evidence: he began to lash it furiously

questions.q: Why did the master say the pony turned toward the park gates?
choices: Sawyer had often driven it there, so it knew the way
The pony was frightened and trying to run away
The pony had seen Black Beauty and wanted to follow him
The pony was hungry and smelled the hay in the park
questions.evidence: it only shows the creature's memory and intelligence

questions.q: What did the master tell Sawyer about losing his temper with the pony?
choices: It hurt Sawyer's own character as much as the horse
It was a good, firm way to train a young and willful pony
It would make the pony go faster in the end
It was not really any of the master's business
questions.evidence: you injure your own character as much, nay more, than you injure your horse

questions.q: Captain Langley wanted to know the master's opinion of what?
choices: His new pair of gray horses
His new carriage and harness
His regiment of soldiers
His new hunting dogs
questions.evidence: What do you think of my new team, Mr. Douglas?

questions.q: Why did the master compare Langley's horses to soldiers with their heads tied to a backboard?
choices: To show that tying heads up takes away strength and freedom
To show that soldiers should ride horses instead of marching
To praise how smart and neat the grays looked in harness
To tell Captain Langley he ought to go back to the army
questions.evidence: you fret and worry their tempers, and decrease their power

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The master and mistress speaking up plainly against cruelty
A long journey to London that the master made with Ginger
How John Manly trained Black Beauty to pull the carriage
A race between two carriages along the road to the village
questions.evidence: there was no oppressed or ill-used creature that had not a friend in them
